The team's coach, the wise and seasoned Juan Carlos, patted Craig on the back, saying, "You're not just a player, Craig, you're a part of our familia." But amidst the city's vibrant atmosphere, Craig's true passion was basketball. He spent countless hours honing his skills on the court, driven by a fierce determination to succeed. In the summer of 2014, Craig made the decision to commit to LSU, choosing to stay close to home and play for the Tigers. It was a move that would prove to be a defining moment in his young career. As Craig arrived on campus, he was greeted by the iconic Pete Maravich Assembly Center, home of the LSU Tigers men's basketball team. The arena, named after the legendary "Pistol" Pete Maravich, was a testament to the rich basketball heritage of the university. Craig knew that he had big shoes to fill, but he was ready to make his mark. Throughout his freshman season, Craig proved to be a valuable asset to the Tigers. He averaged 11.5 points and 5.7 rebounds per game, earning him a spot on the SEC All-Freshman Team. His impressive performance on the court was matched by his dedication in the classroom, where he maintained a strong academic record. As the seasons passed, Craig continued to grow and develop as a player. He became known for his versatility, able to score from both inside and outside the paint, as well as his tenacious rebounding and defensive skills.
